title: Rational Functions
summary: A rational function is a ratio of polynomials. Its domain excludes zeros of the denominator; those give vertical asymptotes or holes. End behavior (from the degrees) gives horizontal or slant asymptotes, and factoring reveals intercepts.

vertical asymptote.plain: A line the graph shoots along.

hole.plain: A removable gap in the graph.
hole.in_class: Where a factor cancels top and bottom.

horizontal asymptote.plain: A level the graph approaches far out.

slant asymptote.in_class: When the top's degree is one more than the bottom's.

domain (rational).plain: All inputs except zeros of the denominator.

concept_sections.heading: Domain and vertical asymptotes
concept_sections.explanation: The domain excludes zeros of the denominator. At those points you get a vertical asymptote (if the numerator isn't also zero there) or a hole (if a factor cancels).

concept_sections.heading: Horizontal asymptotes
concept_sections.explanation: Compare degrees: bottom bigger ⇒ $y=0$; equal ⇒ ratio of leading coefficients; top bigger ⇒ no horizontal asymptote (possibly a slant).
math_steps: Read off the horizontal asymptote (if any).

concept_sections.heading: Slant asymptotes
concept_sections.explanation: When the numerator's degree is exactly one more than the denominator's, long division gives a linear quotient — the slant asymptote.
math_steps: The linear quotient is the slant asymptote.

concept_sections.heading: Intercepts
concept_sections.explanation: The x-intercepts are zeros of the numerator (where the denominator isn't zero); the y-intercept is $R(0)$.
math_steps: Set the numerator to zero for x-intercepts.
Exclude any that zero the denominator.

concept_sections.heading: Sketching
concept_sections.explanation: Combine domain restrictions, asymptotes (vertical, horizontal/slant), holes, and intercepts to sketch the graph piece by piece.
math_steps: Sketch each branch toward the asymptotes.
